tagline: Find any host — and every asset behind a dashboard number.
lore: The Bloodhound, finest tracker of the pack — here it tracks any host across navi.db, and every asset behind a number.
problem: "Which assets is that number?" is the first question after any dashboard — and answering it usually means a hand-written query or an export. Without the list, a metric can't be acted on.
does: Bloodhound searches every asset by hostname, IP, OS or network. It is also where On the Scent's At a glance cards land: each card opens the exact assets behind its number — computed by the hound that owns it — riskiest (highest ACR) first, ready to page, search and export.

glance.caption: Bloodhound opened from an On the Scent card: the evidence card names the number and the hound that owns it, and the asset list below pages and searches on the server and exports to CSV.

capabilities: hostname, IP, OS or network in one box.
KEV-exploitable assets, assets scored 60 or more, crown jewels (all, with KEV, or scanned without credentials), assets flagged by four or more hounds, EOL software, quantum-vulnerable crypto.
each list is computed with the owning hound's own rule — Laelaps, Nemesis, Charon or Heimdall.
the list is stored on the server, so 50 or 150,000 assets page, search and export the same way.
every host opens Argos, where its findings can be remediated with Amarok or tagged; a Tenable link opens it in Tenable.
how: Bloodhound reads your local navi.db and changes nothing. Evidence lists are built on request by the hound that owns the number, so they reflect navi.db now — a card built at the last Release the Hounds run can differ slightly.
who: Analysts and VM leads who need to see — and act on — the assets behind a metric.
better: On the Scent's cards open here; Argos takes over for one asset; Gabriel can email the list.
cta: Give Bloodhound a number — it brings back every asset behind it.
